rounds.prompt: The company's decision showed complete ___ for employee safety.
rounds.note: After ‘complete’ you need a noun; dis- makes it the opposite: no regard at all.

rounds.prompt: She couldn't go out yesterday evening; she had to stay home and look after her younger ___.
rounds.note: After ‘her younger’ a plural noun: relatives (or relations) are family members.

rounds.prompt: After days of ___, they finally found the missing documents.
rounds.note: After ‘days of’ a noun; here the -ing form works as one.

rounds.prompt: His ___ in the competition surprised everyone, including himself.
rounds.note: After ‘His’ a noun: succeed → success.

rounds.prompt: That young lady is very ___ in her work and always meets deadlines.
rounds.note: After ‘very’ an adjective: conscience → conscientious, careful and hard-working.

rounds.prompt: ___ plants are very difficult to grow in the UK climate.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘plants’ an adjective: tropics → tropical.

rounds.prompt: The news came as such a shock that they were both ___.
rounds.note: After ‘were both’ an adjective: -less means without — without speech.

rounds.prompt: I thought the whole evening was very ___.
rounds.note: After ‘very’ an adjective: -able, something you can enjoy.

rounds.prompt: She didn't get the job because she lacked the right ___.
rounds.note: After ‘the right’ a noun, usually plural: qualify → qualifications.

rounds.prompt: You'd like to speak to Mr Smith? That's ___ 342.
rounds.note: A phone number inside a company: extend → extension.

rounds.prompt: The new software offers excellent ___ between all devices.
rounds.note: After ‘excellent’ a noun: connect → connectivity (or connection).

rounds.prompt: You're playing a very ___ game with your personal data.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘game’ an adjective: danger → dangerous.

rounds.prompt: There was a terrific ___ and then the whole building collapsed.
rounds.note: After ‘a terrific’ a noun: explode → explosion.

rounds.prompt: He said 'Good morning' in a most ___ way.
rounds.note: Before ‘way’ an adjective: friend → friendly (or unfriendly). It ends in -ly but it is not an adverb.

rounds.prompt: My teacher ___ me to take the examination.
rounds.note: A past-tense verb after the subject: en- + courage → encouraged.

rounds.prompt: This skirt is too short, so I must have it ___.
rounds.note: have it + past participle: long → lengthen → lengthened.

rounds.prompt: Archaeologists located the walls at a ___ of several metres below the surface.
rounds.note: After ‘a’ a noun: deep → depth.

rounds.prompt: There were scenes of great ___ when the results were announced.
rounds.note: After ‘great’ a noun: excite → excitement.

rounds.prompt: They must accept the ___ of the court.
rounds.note: After ‘the’ a noun: decide → decision.

rounds.prompt: It should always be possible to make a ___ against a government official.
rounds.note: After ‘a’ a noun: complain → complaint.

rounds.prompt: There was no ___ for them to make two separate journeys.
rounds.note: After ‘no’ a noun: necessary → necessity.

rounds.prompt: This dog has been trained to be completely ___ to his master.
rounds.note: After ‘completely’ an adjective: obey → obedient.

rounds.prompt: To guarantee ___ to the course you should apply very early.
rounds.note: After ‘guarantee’ a noun: admit → admission, the right to enter.

rounds.prompt: Her suitcase seemed ___ heavy for such a short trip.
rounds.note: Before the adjective ‘heavy’ an adverb, and negative: un- + necessary + -ly.

rounds.prompt: The two political parties have ___ attitudes to the problem.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘attitudes’ an adjective: oppose → opposing.

rounds.prompt: The boy's ___ improved as he grew older.
rounds.note: After ‘The boy's’ a noun: behave → behaviour.

rounds.prompt: I made him ___ for being so rude.
rounds.note: make someone + verb: apology → apologise.

rounds.prompt: Everybody in this ___ works at the local factory.
rounds.note: After ‘this’ a noun for a place: neighbour → neighbourhood.

rounds.prompt: There is a ___ that life exists on other planets.
rounds.note: After ‘a’ a noun: believe → belief.

rounds.prompt: Although his visit was ___, we made him welcome.
rounds.note: After ‘was’ an adjective, negative: un- + expected.

rounds.prompt: Since he was well trained, winning the race was ___ easy.
rounds.note: Before the adjective ‘easy’ an adverb: compare → comparatively.

rounds.prompt: I should like to hear a ___ of opinions on this matter.
rounds.note: After ‘a’ and before ‘of’ a noun: vary → variety.

rounds.prompt: In his ___ to be understood, he spoke slowly and very loudly.
rounds.note: After ‘his’ a noun: anxious → anxiety.

rounds.prompt: Her writing is very bad. I can't even read her ___.
rounds.note: After ‘her’ a noun: sign → signature, your name written by hand.

rounds.prompt: All classes ___ in January will end in April.
rounds.note: ‘classes beginning in January’: the -ing form after a noun, like a relative clause.

rounds.prompt: You should pack the glasses carefully to avoid ___.
rounds.note: After ‘avoid’ a noun: break → breakage.

rounds.prompt: After most children had gone, the house was ___ quiet.
rounds.note: Before the adjective ‘quiet’ an adverb: compare → comparatively.

rounds.prompt: The cat examined the new food ___.
rounds.note: After the verb and its object an adverb: suspect → suspicious → suspiciously.

rounds.prompt: Now she is earning money she feels more ___.
rounds.note: After ‘more’ an adjective, with a prefix: in- + dependent.

rounds.prompt: The arrested man could give no ___ of his actions.
rounds.note: After ‘no’ a noun: explain → explanation.

rounds.prompt: It is really ___ that we two cousins have never met before.
rounds.note: After ‘really’ an adjective: extra- + ordinary, very unusual.

rounds.prompt: The results of the examination were very ___.
rounds.note: After ‘very’ an adjective: satisfy → satisfactory.

rounds.prompt: They meet and shout and wave banners and applaud their ___.
rounds.note: After ‘their’ a plural noun: lead → leaders.

rounds.prompt: They ___ march long distances in all weathers.
rounds.note: Before the verb ‘march’ an adverb: cheer → cheerful → cheerfully.

rounds.prompt: If necessary, they fight for their ___.
rounds.note: After ‘their’ a plural noun: believe → beliefs.

rounds.prompt: If trouble breaks out, they may be arrested and even ___.
rounds.note: ‘arrested and even ___’: a past participle like ‘arrested’: im- + prison + -ed.

rounds.prompt: Yet it is ___ how much good all this really does.
rounds.note: After ‘it is’ an adjective: doubt → doubtful.

rounds.prompt: They frequently ___ the traffic as they march through the streets.
rounds.note: After ‘frequently’ a verb: im- + mobile + -ise, to stop something moving.

rounds.prompt: They cause trouble and ___ to pedestrians and police.
rounds.note: ‘cause trouble and ___’: a noun like ‘trouble’: irritate → irritation.

rounds.prompt: The result is that people become ___ to their cause.
rounds.note: After ‘become’ an adjective: sympathy → sympathetic (un- if they turn against it).

rounds.prompt: ___ for the movement has declined in recent months.
rounds.note: The subject of the sentence, so a noun: public → publicity.

rounds.prompt: The number of ___ people increases daily.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘people’ an adjective: -less means without a home.

rounds.prompt: However, as yet there seems no satisfactory ___.
rounds.note: After ‘satisfactory’ a noun: solve → solution.

rounds.prompt: The lack of ___ at affordable rents is a disgrace.
rounds.note: After ‘lack of’ a noun: accommodate → accommodation.

rounds.prompt: The ___ of vast office blocks occupies valuable space.
rounds.note: After ‘The’ a noun: erect → erection, the act of building.

rounds.prompt: Such blocks are frequently left ___.
rounds.note: left + adjective, negative: un- + occupied, empty.

rounds.prompt: The ___ of those who have nowhere to live is ignored.
rounds.note: After ‘The’ a noun: miserable → misery.

rounds.prompt: Converting buildings into flats would be ___ for property owners.
rounds.note: After ‘would be’ an adjective: profit → profitable (un- if it brings no profit).

rounds.prompt: Local people must form Housing ___ to help themselves.
rounds.note: After ‘Housing’ a plural noun: associate → associations.

rounds.prompt: The government's ___ to the crisis has been inadequate.
rounds.note: After ‘The government's’ a noun: respond → response.

rounds.prompt: But the prospect of free time seems to discourage them ___.
rounds.note: After the verb and its object an adverb: complete → completely.

rounds.prompt: This is because they are ___ for it.
rounds.note: After ‘are’ an adjective, negative: un- + prepared.

rounds.prompt: If elderly people want to enjoy leisure, they must make proper ___.
rounds.note: make + noun: provide → provision; ‘make provision for’.

rounds.prompt: Whatever they are ___ in, now is the time to enjoy it.
rounds.note: be interested in: the -ed adjective, because it describes how they feel.

rounds.prompt: ___, bird-watching, painting - they must plan well in advance.
rounds.note: In a list of hobbies, a noun: garden → gardening.

rounds.prompt: Many retirees find great ___ in volunteer work.
rounds.note: After ‘great’ a noun: satisfy → satisfaction.

rounds.prompt: Physical ___ is important for maintaining health in retirement.
rounds.note: After ‘Physical’ a noun: active → activity.

rounds.prompt: Some people experience ___ after leaving the workplace.
rounds.note: After ‘experience’ a noun: lonely → loneliness.

rounds.prompt: Proper financial ___ ensures a comfortable retirement.
rounds.note: After ‘financial’ a noun: prepare → preparation.

rounds.prompt: The problem is particularly acute in the ___ countries.
rounds.note: Before ‘countries’ an adjective: developing (or developed).

rounds.prompt: Natural resources are becoming ___ for the increasing population.
rounds.note: After ‘becoming’ an adjective, negative: in- + adequate, not enough.

rounds.prompt: ___ damage is accelerating at an alarming rate.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘damage’ an adjective: environment → environmental.

rounds.prompt: Many species face ___ due to habitat loss.
rounds.note: After ‘face’ a noun: extinct → extinction.

rounds.prompt: ___ advances offer some hope for sustainable solutions.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘advances’ an adjective: technology → technological.

rounds.prompt: ___ between nations is essential to address these challenges.
rounds.note: The subject of the sentence, so a noun: cooperate → cooperation.

rounds.prompt: ___ of resources must be reduced dramatically.
rounds.note: The subject of the sentence, so a noun: consume → consumption.

rounds.prompt: Public awareness campaigns are proving ___.
rounds.note: After ‘proving’ an adjective: effect → effective.

rounds.prompt: Without ___ action, the consequences will be severe.
rounds.note: Before the noun ‘action’ an adjective: urge → urgent.

rounds.prompt: Student ___ has improved since the new policy was introduced.
rounds.note: After ‘Student’ a noun: attend → attendance.

rounds.prompt: Her ___ in mathematics earned her a scholarship.
rounds.note: After ‘Her’ a noun: achieve → achievement.

rounds.prompt: The course offers excellent ___ for university studies.
rounds.note: After ‘excellent’ a noun: prepare → preparation.

rounds.prompt: ___ is the key factor in successful learning.
rounds.note: The subject of the sentence, so a noun: motivate → motivation.

rounds.prompt: The school promotes ___ and respect among students.
rounds.note: Like ‘respect’, a noun: tolerate → tolerance.

rounds.prompt: Technology has revolutionized ___ in recent decades.
rounds.note: The object of ‘revolutionized’, a noun: educate → education.

rounds.prompt: Critical ___ skills are emphasized throughout the curriculum.
rounds.note: ‘Critical ___ skills’: thinking, the -ing noun.

rounds.prompt: The library provides an excellent ___ environment.
rounds.note: Before ‘environment’ a noun used like an adjective: learning environment.

rounds.prompt: ___ methods vary depending on the subject.
rounds.note: Before ‘methods’ a noun used like an adjective: assessment methods.
